story: After initial laps, GC times were taken at the 5th passage of the finish line. Pedersen attacked at the first Montmartre passage, but the peloton stayed intact. Pogačar struck on the second lap, followed only by Van der Poel. Evenepoel and Pedersen joined briefly, but all were caught before the final lap. Van der Poel’s late attack with Pogačar on the last climb of the Tour gave them small lead over a chasing group led by Decathlon CMA CGM for Kooij. With 500 meters to go, and a three second gap, Van der Poel left Pogačar behind, in pursuit of the victory. Behind him, Pedersen launched the sprint, decreasing the gap. Philipsen overtook Pedersen, but Van der Poel narrowly stayed ahead.
